question: Which air brake system applies and releases the brakes when the driver uses the brake pedal during normal driving?
choice_a: Service brake system
choice_b: Parking brake system
explanation: The service brake system applies and releases the brakes when you use the brake pedal during normal driving.
source_note: Tennessee CDL Manual, Section 5.0 - Introduction to Air Brakes

question: The parking brake system applies and releases the parking brakes using what?
choice_a: The brake pedal
choice_b: The parking brake control
explanation: The parking brake system applies and releases the parking brakes when you use the parking brake control.
source_note: Tennessee CDL Manual, Section 5.0 - Introduction to Air Brakes

question: What does the emergency brake system use to stop the vehicle in case of a brake system failure?
choice_a: A completely separate hydraulic system
choice_b: Only the spring brakes on the front axle
choice_c: Parts of the service and parking brake systems
explanation: The emergency brake system uses parts of the service and parking brake systems to stop the vehicle in a brake system failure.
source_note: Tennessee CDL Manual, Section 5.0 - Introduction to Air Brakes

question: How is the air compressor typically connected to the engine?
choice_a: Through the transmission driveshaft
choice_b: Through the electrical system only
explanation: The air compressor is connected to the engine through gears or a v-belt, and may be air cooled or cooled by the engine cooling system.
source_note: Tennessee CDL Manual, Section 5.1.1 - Air Compressor

question: At approximately what pressure does the air compressor governor stop the compressor from pumping air ("cut-out")?
choice_a: 125 psi
choice_b: 55 psi
explanation: When air tank pressure rises to the cut-out level, around 125 psi, the governor stops the compressor from pumping air.
source_note: Tennessee CDL Manual, Section 5.1.2 - Air Compressor Governor

question: At approximately what pressure does the governor allow the air compressor to start pumping again ("cut-in")?
choice_a: 80 psi
choice_b: 100 psi
explanation: When tank pressure falls to the cut-in pressure, around 100 psi, the governor allows the compressor to start pumping again.
source_note: Tennessee CDL Manual, Section 5.1.2 - Air Compressor Governor

question: What is the purpose of air storage tanks in an air brake system?
choice_a: To cool the compressed air
choice_b: To filter oil out of the fuel
choice_c: To hold compressed air so brakes can be used several times even if the compressor stops working
choice_d: To power the parking brake modulating valve
explanation: Air storage tanks hold compressed air, and will hold enough to allow the brakes to be used several times even if the compressor stops working.
source_note: Tennessee CDL Manual, Section 5.1.3 - Air Storage Tanks

question: How must manually operated air tank drain valves be emptied?
choice_a: Automatically by an electric heater
choice_b: Only by a mechanic during scheduled maintenance
choice_d: By turning a quarter turn or pulling a cable, done by the driver at the end of each day
explanation: Manually operated drain valves are opened by a quarter turn or pulling a cable, and the driver must drain the tanks at the end of each day of driving.
source_note: Tennessee CDL Manual, Section 5.1.4 - Air Tank Drains

question: What feature is available on automatic air tanks to help prevent freezing of the drain in cold weather?
choice_a: Electric heating devices
choice_b: A larger safety valve
explanation: Automatic air tanks are available with electric heating devices to help prevent freezing of the automatic drain in cold weather.
source_note: Tennessee CDL Manual, Section 5.1.4 - Air Tank Drains

question: What is the purpose of an alcohol evaporator in an air brake system?
choice_a: To lubricate the s-cam
choice_b: To reduce the risk of ice forming in air brake valves and other parts during cold weather
explanation: An alcohol evaporator puts alcohol into the air system to reduce the risk of ice in air brake valves and other parts during cold weather.
source_note: Tennessee CDL Manual, Section 5.1.5 - Alcohol Evaporator

question: At approximately what pressure is the safety relief valve usually set to open?
choice_a: 100 psi
choice_b: 125 psi
explanation: The safety valve is installed in the first tank the compressor pumps air to and is usually set to open at 150 psi.
source_note: Tennessee CDL Manual, Section 5.1.6 - Safety Valve

question: The brake pedal on an air brake system is also known by what other names?
choice_a: The governor or safety valve
choice_b: The wig wag or modulating valve
choice_d: The foot valve or treadle valve
explanation: The brake pedal is also called the foot valve or treadle valve.
source_note: Tennessee CDL Manual, Section 5.1.7 - The Brake Pedal

question: What can happen if a driver presses and releases the brake pedal unnecessarily?
choice_a: Air can be let out of the system faster than the compressor can replace it, leading to low pressure
choice_b: The alcohol evaporator will overfill
choice_c: The stop light switch will fail permanently
choice_d: The front brake limiting valve will engage automatically
explanation: Pressing and releasing the pedal unnecessarily can let air out faster than the compressor can replace it; if pressure gets too low, the brakes won't work.
source_note: Tennessee CDL Manual, Section 5.1.7 - The Brake Pedal

question: What is the most common type of foundation brake used at each wheel?
choice_a: The wedge brake
choice_b: The s-cam drum brake
explanation: Foundation brakes are used at each wheel, and the most common type is the s-cam drum brake.
source_note: Tennessee CDL Manual, Section 5.1.8 - Foundation Brakes

question: In an s-cam drum brake, what happens when the brake pedal is pushed?
choice_a: Air pressure directly clamps a caliper onto a rotor
choice_b: A wedge is pushed directly between two brake shoes
choice_c: Air pressure pushes a rod out, twisting the camshaft so the s-cam forces the brake shoes against the drum
choice_d: The alcohol evaporator releases fluid onto the shoes
explanation: Air pressure pushes the rod out, moving the slack adjuster and twisting the camshaft, turning the s-cam which forces the brake shoes against the inside of the drum.
source_note: Tennessee CDL Manual, Section 5.1.8 - Foundation Brakes

question: In a wedge brake, what does the brake chamber push rod do?
choice_a: Turns a power screw that clamps a disc
choice_b: Rotates the s-cam
choice_d: Pushes a wedge directly between the ends of two brake shoes, shoving them apart against the drum
explanation: In wedge brakes, the brake chamber push rod pushes a wedge directly between the ends of two brake shoes, shoving them apart and against the inside of the brake drum.
source_note: Tennessee CDL Manual, Section 5.1.8 - Foundation Brakes

question: In air-operated disc brakes, what does the power screw do?
choice_a: Clamps the disc or rotor between the brake lining pads of a caliper, similar to a large c-clamp
choice_b: Pumps compressed air into the storage tanks
choice_c: Controls the low air pressure warning signal
explanation: The power screw clamps the disc or rotor between the brake lining pads of a caliper, similar to a large c-clamp.
source_note: Tennessee CDL Manual, Section 5.1.8 - Foundation Brakes

question: What do supply pressure gauges tell the driver?
choice_a: How much air pressure is being applied to the brakes right now
choice_b: How much pressure is in the air tanks
choice_d: The temperature of the brake drums
explanation: All vehicles with air brakes have a pressure gauge connected to the air tank; these gauges tell you how much pressure is in the air tanks.
source_note: Tennessee CDL Manual, Section 5.1.9 - Supply Pressure Gauges

question: On a vehicle with a dual air brake system, how are supply pressure gauges typically arranged?
choice_a: There is no gauge required
choice_b: A single gauge only shows the primary system
choice_c: There is a gauge for each half of the system, or a single gauge with two needles
choice_d: Only the secondary system has a gauge
explanation: If the vehicle has a dual air brake system, there will be a gauge for each half of the system, or a single gauge with two needles.
source_note: Tennessee CDL Manual, Section 5.1.9 - Supply Pressure Gauges

question: What does the application pressure gauge show?
choice_a: How much air pressure remains in the storage tanks
choice_b: The cut-in and cut-out pressure of the governor
choice_c: The pressure required to release the spring brakes
choice_d: How much air pressure you are applying to the brakes
explanation: The application pressure gauge shows how much air pressure you are applying to the brakes; this gauge is not on all vehicles.
source_note: Tennessee CDL Manual, Section 5.1.10 - Application Pressure Gauge

question: What does it mean if increasing application pressure is needed to hold the same speed?
choice_a: The brakes are fading, and the driver should slow down and use a lower gear
choice_b: The vehicle has an automatic slack adjuster problem only
choice_d: The wig wag device is stuck
explanation: Increasing application pressure to hold the same speed means the brakes are fading; you should slow down and use a lower gear.
source_note: Tennessee CDL Manual, Section 5.1.10 - Application Pressure Gauge

question: A low air pressure warning signal must come on before the air pressure in the tanks falls below what level (on most vehicles)?
choice_a: 100 psi
choice_b: 55 psi
explanation: A warning signal you can see must come on before the air pressure in the tanks falls below 55 psi (or one half the compressor governor cutout pressure on older vehicles).
source_note: Tennessee CDL Manual, Section 5.1.11 - Low Air Pressure Warning

question: What is the "wig wag" warning device?
choice_a: A buzzer that sounds only at start-up
choice_b: A yellow malfunction lamp for ABS
choice_c: A mechanical arm that drops into the driver's view when pressure drops below 55 psi
explanation: The wig wag device drops a mechanical arm into your view when the pressure in the system drops below 55 psi, and rises out of view when pressure goes above 55 psi.
source_note: Tennessee CDL Manual, Section 5.1.11 - Low Air Pressure Warning

question: How does the air brake system warn drivers behind you that you are braking?
choice_a: With a mechanical horn triggered by the s-cam
choice_b: With the wig wag device
choice_d: With an electric switch that works by air pressure and turns on the brake lights
explanation: The air brake system uses an electric switch that works by air pressure to turn on the brake lights when you put on the air brakes.
source_note: Tennessee CDL Manual, Section 5.1.12 - Stop Light Switch

question: What was the purpose of the front brake limiting valve found on some older vehicles (made before 1975)?
choice_a: To reduce the chance of front wheels skidding on slippery surfaces by cutting front brake pressure in half
choice_b: To increase stopping power on dry pavement
choice_c: To engage the spring brakes automatically
explanation: When placed in the slippery position, the limiting valve cuts the normal air pressure to the front brakes by half, intended to reduce front wheel skidding on slippery surfaces.
source_note: Tennessee CDL Manual, Section 5.1.13 - Front Brake Limiting Valve

question: Why are spring brakes typically used for the emergency and parking brake systems?
choice_a: Because they are cheaper than air chambers
choice_b: Because they must be held on by mechanical force, since air pressure can eventually leak away
choice_c: Because they only work on front axles
choice_d: Because they eliminate the need for a governor
explanation: Emergency and parking brakes must be held on by mechanical force because air pressure can eventually leak away; spring brakes are usually used to meet this need.
source_note: Tennessee CDL Manual, Section 5.1.14 - Spring Brakes

question: How do spring brakes apply the brakes?
choice_a: Air pressure directly pushes the brake shoes against the drum
choice_b: A hydraulic fluid actuates the shoes
choice_c: Powerful springs are held back by air pressure; if air pressure is removed, the springs put on the brakes
choice_d: The alcohol evaporator releases fluid to engage the springs
explanation: When driving, powerful springs are held back by air pressure; if the air pressure is removed, the springs put on the brakes.
source_note: Tennessee CDL Manual, Section 5.1.14 - Spring Brakes

question: At what pressure range will tractor and straight truck spring brakes come fully on?
choice_a: 100 to 125 psi
choice_b: 55 to 80 psi
explanation: Tractor and straight truck spring brakes will come fully on when air pressure drops to a range of 20 to 45 psi, typically 20 to 30 psi.
source_note: Tennessee CDL Manual, Section 5.1.14 - Spring Brakes

question: What should a driver do when the low air pressure warning light and buzzer first come on?
choice_a: Bring the vehicle to a safe stop right away, while brakes can still be controlled
choice_b: Continue driving normally since spring brakes will engage automatically
choice_c: Increase speed to reach a repair facility faster
choice_d: Switch the front brake limiting valve to "slippery"
explanation: Do not wait for the brakes to come on automatically; bring the vehicle to a safe stop right away while you can still control the brakes.
source_note: Tennessee CDL Manual, Section 5.1.14 - Spring Brakes

question: What does the braking power of spring brakes depend on?
choice_a: The color of the parking brake knob
choice_b: The brakes being in proper adjustment
choice_d: The size of the safety valve
explanation: The braking power of spring brakes depends on the brakes being in adjustment; if not adjusted properly, neither the regular brakes nor the emergency/parking brakes will work right.
source_note: Tennessee CDL Manual, Section 5.1.14 - Spring Brakes

question: In newer vehicles with air brakes, how do you apply the parking brakes using the push-pull control knob?
choice_a: Push the diamond-shaped yellow knob in
choice_b: Turn the round blue knob a quarter turn
choice_c: Pull the diamond-shaped yellow knob out
explanation: You pull the diamond-shaped, yellow, push-pull control knob out to apply the parking brakes (spring brakes), and push it in to release them.
source_note: Tennessee CDL Manual, Section 5.1.15 - Parking Brake Controls

question: What caution does the manual give about the brake pedal and spring brakes?
choice_a: Always push the brake pedal down when parking to reinforce the spring brakes
choice_b: The brake pedal has no effect when spring brakes are engaged
choice_c: The brake pedal should be held down while draining air tanks
choice_d: Never push the brake pedal down when the spring brakes are on, as this could damage the brakes
explanation: Never push the brake pedal down when the spring brakes are on; the brakes could be damaged by the combined forces of the springs and the air pressure.
source_note: Tennessee CDL Manual, Section 5.1.15 - Parking Brake Controls

question: What is a modulating control valve used for?
choice_a: To apply the spring brakes gradually using a spring-loaded dash control handle
choice_b: To automatically drain air tanks
choice_d: To cut air pressure to the front brakes in half
explanation: A modulating valve lets a driver apply the spring brakes gradually using a control handle on the dashboard; the more the lever moves, the harder the spring brakes come on.
source_note: Tennessee CDL Manual, Section 5.1.15 - Parking Brake Controls

question: Truck tractors with air brakes built on or after what date are required to be equipped with antilock brakes?
choice_a: March 1, 1998
choice_b: March 1, 1997
explanation: Truck tractors with air brakes built on or after March 1, 1997 are required to be equipped with antilock brakes.
source_note: Tennessee CDL Manual, Section 5.1.16 - Antilock Braking Systems

question: Other air brake vehicles (trucks, buses, trailers, and converter dollies) are required to have ABS if built on or after what date?
choice_a: March 1, 1997
choice_b: May 2022
explanation: Other air brakes vehicles (trucks, buses, trailers, and converter dollies) built on or after March 1, 1998 are required to be equipped with antilock brakes.
source_note: Tennessee CDL Manual, Section 5.1.16 - Antilock Braking Systems

question: What color are the ABS malfunction lamps required on vehicles equipped with ABS?
choice_a: Red
choice_b: Blue
explanation: Vehicles with ABS have yellow malfunction lamps to tell you if something isn't working.
source_note: Tennessee CDL Manual, Section 5.1.16 - Antilock Braking Systems

question: Where are yellow ABS malfunction lamps located on trailers?
choice_a: On the left side, either on the front or rear corner
choice_b: On the instrument panel
explanation: Trailers will have yellow ABS malfunction lamps on the left side, either on the front or rear corner.
source_note: Tennessee CDL Manual, Section 5.1.16 - Antilock Braking Systems

question: According to the manual, what does ABS do?
choice_a: It decreases normal braking capability in exchange for stability
choice_b: It is an addition to normal brakes that activates only when wheels are about to lock up
choice_d: It replaces the need for spring brakes
explanation: ABS is an addition to your normal brakes; it does not decrease or increase normal braking capability and only activates when wheels are about to lock up.
source_note: Tennessee CDL Manual, Section 5.1.16 - Antilock Braking Systems

question: Does ABS necessarily shorten stopping distance?
choice_a: Yes, always by at least 30 feet
choice_b: Yes, but only on wet pavement
choice_c: No, but it helps keep the vehicle under control during hard braking
choice_d: No, ABS has no effect on control or stopping distance
explanation: ABS does not necessarily shorten your stopping distance, but it does help you keep the vehicle under control during hard braking.
source_note: Tennessee CDL Manual, Section 5.1.16 - Antilock Braking Systems

question: What is a dual air brake system?
choice_a: A system with two brake pedals for the driver and passenger
choice_b: A system that uses both hydraulic and air brakes simultaneously
choice_c: A system with two safety valves on one tank
choice_d: Two separate air brake systems that use a single set of brake controls, each with its own tanks, hoses, and lines
explanation: A dual air brake system has two separate air brake systems, which use a single set of brake controls; each system has its own air tanks, hoses, lines, etc.
source_note: Tennessee CDL Manual, Section 5.2 - Dual Air Brake Systems

question: In a dual air brake system, what are the two systems typically called?
choice_a: Primary and secondary
choice_b: Front and rear
explanation: One system is called the primary system and the other is called the secondary system; one typically operates the rear axle brakes, the other the front axle brakes.
source_note: Tennessee CDL Manual, Section 5.2 - Dual Air Brake Systems

question: Before driving a vehicle with a dual air system, the air compressor should build up a minimum of what pressure in both systems?
choice_a: 55 psi
choice_b: 100 psi
explanation: Before driving a vehicle with a dual air system, allow time for the air compressor to build up a minimum of 100 psi pressure in both the primary and secondary systems.
source_note: Tennessee CDL Manual, Section 5.2 - Dual Air Brake Systems

question: If one air system in a dual air brake setup is very low on pressure, what happens?
choice_a: Nothing, the other system fully compensates
choice_b: The safety valve automatically releases at 150 psi
choice_c: Either the front or rear brakes will not be operating fully, meaning it takes longer to stop
explanation: If one air system is very low on pressure, either the front or the rear brakes will not be operating fully, meaning it will take longer to stop.
source_note: Tennessee CDL Manual, Section 5.2 - Dual Air Brake Systems

question: When checking slack adjusters on s-cam brakes, if a slack adjuster moves more than about how far where the push rod attaches, it probably needs adjustment?
choice_a: One quarter inch
choice_b: Three inches
explanation: If a slack adjuster moves more than about one inch where the push rod attaches to it, it probably needs adjustment.
source_note: Tennessee CDL Manual, Section 5.3.2 - Walk-around Inspection

question: Vehicles built since what year have automatic slack adjustors?
explanation: All vehicles built since 1994 have automatic slack adjustors.
source_note: Tennessee CDL Manual, Section 5.3.2 - Walk-around Inspection

question: Why is manually adjusting an automatic slack adjuster considered risky according to the manual?
choice_a: It voids the vehicle's warranty
choice_b: It only masks the underlying mechanical problem and can give a false sense of security about the brakes
choice_c: It permanently disables the ABS system
choice_d: It causes the safety valve to fail
explanation: Manual adjustment of an automatic adjuster generally masks a mechanical problem rather than fixing it, and is dangerous because it may give a false sense of security.
source_note: Tennessee CDL Manual, Section 5.3.2 - Walk-around Inspection

question: Brake drums (or discs) must not have cracks longer than what portion of the width of the friction area?
choice_a: One quarter
choice_b: Three quarters
explanation: Brake drums (or discs) must not have cracks longer than one half the width of the friction area.
source_note: Tennessee CDL Manual, Section 5.3.2 - Walk-around Inspection

question: During the final air brake check, pumping by the air compressor should start at about what pressure and stop at about what pressure?
choice_a: Start at about 55 psi, stop at about 100 psi
choice_b: Start at about 125 psi, stop at about 150 psi
choice_c: Start at about 20 psi, stop at about 45 psi
choice_d: Start at about 100 psi, stop at about 125 psi
explanation: Pumping by the air compressor should start at about 100 psi and stop at about 125 psi (check manufacturer's specifications).
source_note: Tennessee CDL Manual, Section 5.3.3 - Final Air Brake Check

question: With a fully-charged air system and the engine off, what is the maximum acceptable air pressure loss rate for a single vehicle?
choice_a: Less than two psi in one minute
choice_b: Less than three psi in one minute
choice_c: Less than five psi in one minute
choice_d: Less than one psi in thirty seconds
explanation: The loss rate should be less than two psi in one minute for single vehicles and less than three psi in one minute for combination vehicles.
source_note: Tennessee CDL Manual, Section 5.3.3 - Final Air Brake Check

question: What is the maximum acceptable air leakage rate for a combination vehicle with a fully-charged air system?
choice_a: Less than one psi in one minute
choice_b: Less than three psi in one minute
choice_c: Less than two psi in one minute
choice_d: Less than four psi in one minute
explanation: The loss rate should be less than three psi in one minute for combination vehicles.
source_note: Tennessee CDL Manual, Section 5.3.3 - Final Air Brake Check

question: The low air pressure warning signal must come on before the pressure drops below what level in the tank with the lowest pressure?
choice_a: 100 psi
choice_b: 80 psi
explanation: The low air pressure warning signal must come on before the pressure drops to less than 55 psi in the air tank (or tank with the lowest air pressure, in dual air systems).
source_note: Tennessee CDL Manual, Section 5.3.3 - Final Air Brake Check

question: When checking the rate of air pressure buildup in a dual air system at operating rpm, the pressure should build from 85 to 100 psi within how long?
choice_a: 15 seconds
choice_b: 90 seconds
explanation: When the engine is at operating rpms, the pressure should build from 85 to 100 psi within 45 seconds in dual air systems.
source_note: Tennessee CDL Manual, Section 5.3.3 - Final Air Brake Check

question: How should a driver test the parking brake during inspection?
choice_a: By stopping the vehicle, applying the parking brake, and gently pulling against it in a low gear
choice_b: By checking the alcohol evaporator level
choice_c: By measuring the slack adjuster travel
choice_d: By pushing the treadle valve fully to the floor
explanation: Stop the vehicle, put the parking brake on, and gently pull against it in a low gear to test that the parking brake will hold.
source_note: Tennessee CDL Manual, Section 5.3.3 - Final Air Brake Check

question: What is the controlled braking method for emergency stops?
choice_a: Applying the brakes all the way and releasing when wheels lock
choice_b: Applying the brakes as hard as possible without locking the wheels, keeping steering movements small
explanation: With controlled braking, you apply the brakes as hard as you can without locking the wheels, keeping steering wheel movements very small.
source_note: Tennessee CDL Manual, Section 5.4.3 - Emergency Stops

question: What is the stab braking method for emergency stops?
choice_a: Apply light, steady pressure throughout the stop
choice_b: Alternate between the parking brake and service brake
choice_c: Apply brakes all the way, release when wheels lock up, and reapply fully as soon as wheels start rolling again
choice_d: Use only engine braking, never the foot pedal
explanation: Stab braking means applying the brakes all the way, releasing when the wheels lock up, and applying the brakes fully again as soon as the wheels start rolling.
source_note: Tennessee CDL Manual, Section 5.4.3 - Emergency Stops

question: What four factors make up total stopping distance for a vehicle with air brakes?
choice_a: Reaction, Braking, Coasting, and Parking Distance
choice_b: Perception, Governor Cut-in, Cut-out, and Braking Distance
choice_c: Air Leakage, Reaction, Perception, and Coasting Distance
choice_d: Perception, Reaction, Brake Lag, and Braking Distance
explanation: Total Stopping Distance is made up of Perception Distance + Reaction Distance + Brake Lag Distance + Braking Distance.
source_note: Tennessee CDL Manual, Section 5.4.4 - Stopping Distance

question: What is "brake lag" as it relates to air brakes?
choice_a: The time required for the brakes to work after the brake pedal is pushed, due to air needing to flow through the lines
choice_b: The delay before the low pressure warning buzzer sounds
choice_c: The time it takes the governor to cut out
choice_d: The delay in the ABS malfunction lamp bulb check
explanation: With air brakes, brake lag is the added delay - it takes a little time (one half second or more) for the air to flow through the lines to the brakes.
source_note: Tennessee CDL Manual, Section 5.4.4 - Stopping Distance

question: About how much distance does the air brake lag add at 55 mph on dry pavement?
choice_a: About 10 feet
choice_b: About 32 feet
explanation: The air brake lag distance at 55 mph on dry pavement adds about 32 feet.
source_note: Tennessee CDL Manual, Section 5.4.4 - Stopping Distance

question: What causes brake fade?
choice_a: Cold weather reducing air pressure
choice_b: Using the parking brake too often
choice_c: Excessive heat from overuse causing chemical changes in the brake lining and drum expansion
explanation: Excessive use of the service brakes results in overheating and brake fade; brake fade results from excessive heat causing chemical changes in the lining and expansion of the drums.
source_note: Tennessee CDL Manual, Section 5.4.5 - Brake Fading or Failure

question: What is the proper braking technique on a long or steep downgrade, once the vehicle is in the proper low gear?
choice_a: Ride the brakes continuously and lightly
choice_b: Use the parking brake instead of the service brakes
choice_c: Pump the brakes rapidly the entire way down
choice_d: Apply the brakes just hard enough to feel a definite slowdown, then release when reduced about 5 mph below safe speed, and repeat
explanation: Apply the brakes just hard enough to feel a definite slowdown; when speed is reduced to about five mph below your safe speed, release the brakes, and repeat as needed.
source_note: Tennessee CDL Manual, Section 5.4.6 - Proper Braking Technique

question: According to the manual, the use of brakes on a long or steep downgrade is only what?
choice_a: A supplement to the braking effect of the engine
choice_b: The primary method of control, replacing engine braking
explanation: The use of brakes on a long and/or steep downgrade is only a supplement to the braking effect of the engine.
source_note: Tennessee CDL Manual, Section 5.4.6 - Proper Braking Technique

question: If the low air pressure warning comes on while driving, what should the driver do?
choice_a: Continue to destination since spring brakes provide backup
choice_b: Stop and safely park the vehicle as soon as possible
choice_d: Switch the modulating valve to release position
explanation: If the low air pressure warning comes on, stop and safely park your vehicle as soon as possible, as there might be an air leak in the system.
source_note: Tennessee CDL Manual, Section 5.4.7 - Low Air Pressure

question: Why should a driver avoid using the parking brakes when the brakes are very hot, such as after coming down a steep grade?
choice_a: It triggers the ABS malfunction lamp
choice_b: It causes the alcohol evaporator to overflow
choice_c: The hot brakes can be damaged by the heat
explanation: Don't use the parking brakes if the brakes are very hot; if used while very hot, they can be damaged by the heat.
source_note: Tennessee CDL Manual, Section 5.4.8 - Parking Brakes

question: Why should a driver avoid using the parking brakes if they are very wet in freezing temperatures?
choice_a: It will drain the secondary air system
choice_b: It causes rearward amplification
choice_c: It disables the tractor protection valve
choice_d: The brakes can freeze so the vehicle cannot move
explanation: If the parking brakes are used in freezing temperatures when very wet, they can freeze so the vehicle cannot move; wheel chocks should be used instead.
source_note: Tennessee CDL Manual, Section 5.4.8 - Parking Brakes

question: What should a driver never do when leaving a vehicle unattended?
choice_a: Leave without applying the parking brakes or chocking the wheels
choice_b: Turn off the engine
explanation: Never leave your vehicle unattended without applying the parking brakes or chocking the wheels, as it might roll away and cause injury or damage.
source_note: Tennessee CDL Manual, Section 5.4.8 - Parking Brakes
